scenario.title: Submitting leaves the balance unchanged; approving a 3-day range that includes a weekend deducts 3 days
scenario.intent: Sign in as the employee 'emp'. On the "My time off" screen, record the displayed days remaining as observation screenBalanceBefore. Call GET /api/me and record its balance field as apiBalanceBefore. Submit a time-off request with first day 2027-01-08, last day 2027-01-10 (Friday to Sunday) and any reason. Then call GET /api/me again and record balance as apiBalanceAfterSubmit. Call GET /api/requests and find the new request; keep its id and check its status field. Sign out, sign in as the manager 'mgr', and approve that request (in the UI or via POST /api/requests/:id/decision with decision approve). Sign out, sign in again as 'emp', call GET /api/me and record balance as apiBalanceAfterApprove.

assertions.description: Before any request: the days-remaining number shown on the employee's "My time off" screen (screenBalanceBefore) equals the balance returned by GET /api/me at the same moment (apiBalanceBefore).
Right after submitting the 2027-01-08..2027-01-10 request (still pending): GET /api/me balance (apiBalanceAfterSubmit) equals apiBalanceBefore.
Right after submitting, before any manager action: the status field of the new request in GET /api/requests (employee session) contains the text Pending.

After the manager approved the request: GET /api/me balance in a fresh employee session (apiBalanceAfterApprove) equals apiBalanceBefore minus 3 (2027-01-08 to 2027-01-10 inclusive is 3 calendar days, weekend counted).

scenario.title: Rejecting leaves the balance unchanged, and a rejected request cannot later be approved
scenario.intent: Sign in as the employee 'emp', call GET /api/me and record balance as apiBalanceBefore. Submit a single-day request with first and last day 2027-02-03 and any reason. Call GET /api/requests and keep the new request's id. Sign out, sign in as the manager 'mgr' and reject that request (in the UI or via POST /api/requests/:id/decision with decision reject). Sign out, sign in as 'emp', call GET /api/me and record balance as apiBalanceAfterReject. Sign out, sign in as 'mgr' again and send POST /api/requests/:id/decision with decision approve for the same request (a second decision; its response is not itself asserted). Sign out, sign in as 'emp', call GET /api/me and record balance as apiBalanceAfterSecondDecision.

assertions.description: After the manager rejected the request (before the second decision attempt): GET /api/me balance in a fresh employee session (apiBalanceAfterReject) equals apiBalanceBefore.

After the manager's later approve attempt on the already-rejected request: GET /api/me balance in a fresh employee session (apiBalanceAfterSecondDecision) equals apiBalanceAfterReject (a decided request cannot be decided again, so no deduction happens).

scenario.title: Employee cannot decide own request; approval deducts once even if approved twice
scenario.intent: Sign in as the employee 'emp', call GET /api/me and record balance as apiBalanceBefore. Submit a single-day request with first and last day 2027-03-10 and any reason, then read GET /api/requests and keep the new request's id. Still as the employee, send POST /api/requests/:id/decision with decision approve for that request. Then call GET /api/me and record balance as apiBalanceAfterEmployeeDecide, and read the request's status in GET /api/requests. Sign out, sign in as the manager 'mgr' and approve the request. Then, still as manager, send POST /api/requests/:id/decision with decision approve again for the same request. Sign out, sign in as 'emp', call GET /api/me and record balance as apiBalanceFinal.

assertions.description: After the employee tried to approve their own request via the API: GET /api/me balance (apiBalanceAfterEmployeeDecide) equals apiBalanceBefore.
After the employee's own decision attempt: the request's status field in GET /api/requests (employee session) still contains the text Pending.

After the manager approved the single-day request and then sent a second approve: GET /api/me balance in a fresh employee session (apiBalanceFinal) equals apiBalanceBefore minus 1 (one calendar day deducted exactly once).

scenario.title: Approving a request for more days than the employee has remaining
scenario.intent: Employee with 20 days submits a request spanning more than 20 calendar days; manager approves it; inspect the resulting balance.

scenarios.blockedReason: It is not decided whether submitting or approving a request larger than the remaining balance is allowed, and whether the balance may go negative, be capped, or the action be refused.

scenario.title: Overlapping or past-dated requests both approved
scenario.intent: Employee submits two requests covering overlapping dates (or a past-dated request); manager approves both; inspect the balance.

scenarios.blockedReason: It is not decided whether overlapping or past-dated requests are allowed, or whether shared days are deducted twice on approval.

scenario.title: Invalid calendar dates, very long ranges, and end-before-start ranges
scenario.intent: Employee submits requests with an impossible date (e.g. 2027-02-30), a range spanning many months, and a last day before the first day; inspect the responses and the balance.

scenarios.blockedReason: The expected handling of invalid dates and very long ranges is undecided (Q5), and refusing end-before-start ranges (R13) is only an inferred requirement, not documented.
